name: Out of Africa Migration
description: The initial dispersal of anatomically modern humans from East Africa through the Levant and into Asia, Oceania, and eventually all continents
consequences: Colonization of all habitable continents; foundation of all subsequent human genetic and linguistic diversity

name: Indo-European Expansion
description: Migration of Indo-European speaking peoples from the Pontic-Caspian steppe westward into Europe and southeastward into Iran and India
consequences: Spread of Indo-European language family; displacement/assimilation of pre-IE languages; foundation of most European and many Asian languages

name: Bantu Expansion
description: The migration of Bantu-speaking peoples from West-Central Africa across sub-Saharan Africa over several millennia
consequences: Spread of Bantu languages across most of sub-Saharan Africa; spread of iron-working and agriculture; displacement of Khoisan and Pygmy populations

name: Austronesian Expansion
description: Maritime expansion from Taiwan through Island Southeast Asia, Melanesia, and into Polynesia
consequences: Colonization of the Pacific Islands; development of advanced navigation techniques; spread of Austronesian languages to become the most geographically widespread language family

name: Polynesian Voyaging
description: Long-distance oceanic voyaging that settled the Polynesian Triangle from Samoa/Tonga to Hawaii, Easter Island, and New Zealand
consequences: Settlement of the most remote inhabited islands on Earth; development of stellar navigation; cultural diversification across the Pacific

name: Silk Road
description: The ancient network of trade routes connecting East Asia with the Mediterranean, facilitating exchange of goods, ideas, religions, and technologies
consequences: Spread of Buddhism, Islam, and Christianity; transmission of papermaking, gunpowder, and printing; cultural exchange between civilizations; spread of plague

name: Trans-Saharan Trade Routes
description: Trade routes crossing the Sahara Desert connecting North Africa with West Africa, exchanging gold, salt, slaves, and ideas
consequences: Spread of Islam to West Africa; growth of wealthy West African empires (Ghana, Mali, Songhai); trans-continental economic integration

name: Amber Road
description: Ancient trade route connecting the Baltic Sea coast to the Mediterranean, primarily trading amber
consequences: Cultural exchange between Northern and Southern Europe; spread of Roman goods and influence northward; economic interconnection of European regions

name: Incense Route
description: Trade route carrying frankincense and myrrh from southern Arabia to the Mediterranean via the Nabataean kingdom
consequences: Rise of wealthy trading kingdoms in Arabia; cultural exchange between Arabia and the Mediterranean; growth of Petra and other trading cities

name: Viking Expansion
description: Norse seafaring expansion from Scandinavia to Britain, Iceland, Greenland, and briefly North America (Vinland)
consequences: Settlement of Iceland and Greenland; brief contact with Americas; Norse cultural and linguistic influence on English; establishment of Danelaw; Varangian Guard in Byzantium

name: Viking Eastern Route
description: Norse trade and settlement route from Scandinavia through Russia to Constantinople and the Caspian
consequences: Foundation of Kievan Rus; establishment of trade networks connecting Scandinavia to Byzantium and the Islamic world; cultural fusion of Norse and Slavic traditions

name: Arab-Islamic Expansion
description: Rapid military and religious expansion from the Arabian Peninsula across the Middle East, North Africa, Central Asia, and Iberia
consequences: Spread of Islam and Arabic language; creation of vast caliphates; transmission of Greek knowledge; golden age of Islamic science; arabization of North Africa

name: Mongol Conquests
description: The largest contiguous land empire in history, conquering from China to Eastern Europe under Genghis Khan and his successors
consequences: Pax Mongolica enabling trade; destruction of many cities; demographic catastrophe in Central Asia and Persia; fall of Abbasid Caliphate; connection of East and West; spread of plague

name: European Atlantic Colonization
description: Spanish and Portuguese colonization of the Americas following Columbus's 1492 voyage
consequences: Columbian Exchange; destruction of indigenous empires; introduction of European languages, diseases, and cultures; transatlantic slave trade; creation of mestizo societies

name: European Asian Colonization
description: European maritime colonization of coastal Asia from Goa to the Spice Islands, India, and Southeast Asia
consequences: Establishment of colonial trade empires; spread of European languages; transformation of Asian economies; cultural exchange and conflict; rise of English as global lingua franca

name: Atlantic Slave Trade Routes
description: Forced transportation of millions of Africans across the Atlantic to the Americas
consequences: Creation of African diaspora cultures; development of creole languages; African cultural influence on Americas; demographic transformation of the Americas and Africa

name: Jewish Diaspora
description: The dispersion of Jewish people from the Land of Israel following the Roman destruction of the Temple, spreading throughout the Mediterranean, Europe, and beyond
consequences: Development of distinct Jewish communities (Ashkenazi, Sephardi, Mizrahi); creation of Yiddish and Ladino; preservation of Hebrew as liturgical language; cultural contributions across host societies

name: Romani Migration
description: Migration of the Romani people from northern India through Persia, the Byzantine Empire, and into Europe
consequences: Development of Romani language with layers of borrowings from Persian, Greek, and European languages; cultural distinctiveness maintained across centuries; marginalization in European societies

name: Great Migration (US)
description: Mass movement of approximately 6 million African Americans from the rural Southern United States to cities in the North, Midwest, and West
consequences: Transformation of American cities; development of jazz, blues, and other cultural forms; civil rights movement; demographic reshaping of American politics and culture

name: Indo-Aryan Migration
description: Migration of Indo-Aryan peoples from the Central Asian steppes through Afghanistan into the Indian subcontinent
consequences: Spread of Vedic culture and Sanskrit; development of Hindu religion; displacement of Dravidian languages to southern India; caste system development

name: Turkic Migrations
description: Westward migration of Turkic peoples from Central Asia through Persia into Anatolia and beyond
consequences: Turkification of Anatolia; establishment of Ottoman Empire; displacement of Greek and Armenian populations; spread of Turkic languages across Central and Western Asia

name: Crusades
description: Military campaigns by Western European Christians to capture and hold the Holy Land
consequences: Cultural exchange between Europe and the Islamic world; introduction of Eastern goods to Europe; establishment of military orders; increased maritime trade; deterioration of Christian-Muslim relations

name: Portuguese Maritime Route to India
description: Vasco da Gama's sea route around the Cape of Good Hope to India, establishing direct European maritime trade with Asia
consequences: Bypass of overland trade routes and Muslim intermediaries; Portuguese trading empire in Indian Ocean; introduction of European naval power to Asian waters; global maritime trade network

name: Spice Trade Maritime Routes
description: Maritime trade routes connecting South Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Spice Islands, carrying cloves, nutmeg, pepper, and cinnamon
consequences: Economic driver of maritime empires; motivation for European age of exploration; cultural exchange across Indian and Pacific Oceans; spread of Islam to Southeast Asia

name: Trail of Tears
description: Forced relocation of Native American nations from southeastern United States to Indian Territory (Oklahoma)
consequences: Devastating loss of life; destruction of indigenous communities; cultural disruption; legal precedents regarding indigenous rights; intergenerational trauma

name: Phoenician Trade Network
description: Phoenician maritime trading network spanning the entire Mediterranean, establishing colonies including Carthage
consequences: Spread of the Phoenician alphabet (ancestor of Greek, Latin, Arabic scripts); establishment of Carthage; cultural exchange across Mediterranean; development of maritime commerce

name: Han Dynasty Expansion
description: Military expansion of the Han Dynasty westward into Central Asia, establishing control over Silk Road routes
consequences: Opening of Silk Road; Chinese influence in Central Asia; cultural exchange with Rome; spread of Chinese goods and technology westward; establishment of tributary system

name: Irish Diaspora
description: Mass emigration from Ireland, primarily during and after the Great Famine, to North America, Britain, and Australia
consequences: Irish cultural influence in diaspora countries; political movements (Fenian, Home Rule); transformation of American cities; maintenance of Irish identity abroad

name: Malay Archipelago Trade
description: Maritime trade networks throughout the Malay Archipelago connecting India, China, and the Spice Islands
consequences: Spread of Hinduism and Buddhism, then Islam to Southeast Asia; development of maritime Malay as lingua franca; growth of trading sultanates; cultural synthesis of Indian, Chinese, and local traditions

name: Early Human Migration to Europe
description: Migration of modern humans from the Levant into Europe, eventually replacing Neanderthal populations
consequences: Replacement of Neanderthals; cave art traditions; development of European hunter-gatherer cultures; genetic admixture with Neanderthals

name: Beringia Land Bridge Migration
description: Migration of humans from Siberia across the Bering land bridge into the Americas during the last Ice Age
consequences: Colonization of the Americas; development of diverse indigenous cultures and languages; extinction of Pleistocene megafauna; independent invention of agriculture

name: Arab Indian Ocean Trade
description: Arab maritime trade in the Indian Ocean connecting the Arabian Peninsula with the East African coast
consequences: Spread of Islam to East Africa; development of Swahili language and culture; establishment of trading city-states (Kilwa, Zanzibar, Mombasa); cultural fusion of Arab and Bantu traditions

name: Gothic Migrations
description: Migration of Gothic peoples from Scandinavia and the Baltic through Eastern Europe and into the Roman Empire
consequences: Sack of Rome; establishment of Visigothic kingdom in Iberia and Ostrogothic kingdom in Italy; contribution to fall of Western Roman Empire; Gothic influence on Romance languages

name: Hungarian Migration
description: Migration of the Magyar people from the Ural-Volga region across the Pontic steppe into the Carpathian Basin
consequences: Establishment of the Kingdom of Hungary; introduction of a Uralic language into Central Europe surrounded by Indo-European speakers; Hungarian raids across Europe before settling

name: Dravidian Migration
description: Migration of Dravidian-speaking peoples across the Indian subcontinent, predating the Indo-Aryan arrival
consequences: Establishment of Dravidian language family across southern India; development of Indus Valley-linked cultures; rich literary traditions in Tamil and other Dravidian languages

name: Uralic Migration
description: Dispersal of Uralic-speaking peoples from the Ural Mountains region westward into Scandinavia and the Baltic
consequences: Spread of Uralic languages including Finnish, Estonian, Sami, and Hungarian; development of distinct Finno-Ugric and Samoyedic branches

name: Na-Dene Migration
description: Migration of Na-Dene speaking peoples from Alaska and northwestern Canada southward to the American Southwest
consequences: Spread of Athabaskan languages across western North America; later Navajo and Apache settlement in the Southwest; distinct linguistic island amid other language families

name: Celtic Expansion
description: Expansion of Celtic-speaking peoples from Central Europe across Western Europe to Britain, Ireland, and Iberia
consequences: Spread of Celtic languages and La Tene culture; Celtic place names across Europe; later contraction to Atlantic fringe under Roman and Germanic pressure

name: Greek Colonization
description: Greek establishment of colonies across the Mediterranean and Black Sea coasts
consequences: Spread of Greek language and culture; foundation of cities like Marseille, Syracuse, and Byzantium; dissemination of Greek alphabet; cultural exchange with indigenous peoples

name: Khmer Empire Expansion
description: Expansion of the Khmer Empire from Angkor across mainland Southeast Asia
consequences: Spread of Hinduism and Buddhism in Southeast Asia; monumental architecture tradition; Khmer cultural and linguistic influence across the region; hydraulic engineering innovations

name: Norse Atlantic Settlement
description: Norse settlement of the North Atlantic islands from Norway to Iceland, Greenland, and briefly Vinland
consequences: Establishment of Icelandic literary tradition; preservation of Old Norse language; Althing democracy; brief European contact with North America centuries before Columbus

name: Sahel Pastoral Migration
description: Migration of pastoral peoples across the Sahel belt of Africa as the Sahara dried
consequences: Spread of pastoral cultures and languages across West Africa; development of transhumance patterns; Fulani dispersal across the Sahel; adaptation to semi-arid environments

name: Tibetan Plateau Settlement
description: Settlement of the Tibetan Plateau by Tibeto-Burman speaking peoples from the eastern Himalayan region
consequences: Adaptation to high-altitude living; development of Tibetan culture and Buddhism; linguistic diversification of Tibeto-Burman family; isolation preserving archaic linguistic features

name: Roman Expansion
description: Military expansion of the Roman Republic and Empire across the Mediterranean, Western Europe, and Near East
consequences: Spread of Latin leading to Romance languages; Roman law and governance traditions; road networks; urbanization; Christianity; lasting cultural unification of Mediterranean world

name: Macedonian Conquests
description: Alexander the Great's military campaigns from Greece through Persia to Central Asia and India
consequences: Hellenistic cultural diffusion; Greek as lingua franca of eastern Mediterranean; foundation of Alexandria; cultural synthesis of Greek and Eastern traditions; Hellenistic kingdoms

name: Arab-Berber Conquest of Iberia
description: Muslim conquest and settlement of the Iberian Peninsula from North Africa
consequences: Arabic loanwords in Spanish and Portuguese; architectural legacy (Alhambra); convivencia period of coexistence; scientific and philosophical transmission to Europe; Reconquista shaping Iberian identity

name: Japanese Archipelago Settlement
description: Settlement of the Japanese archipelago by Jomon hunter-gatherers and later Yayoi agriculturalists from the Korean Peninsula
consequences: Development of Japanese language through Jomon-Yayoi interaction; displacement of Ainu to northern islands; wet rice agriculture; formation of Japanese cultural identity

name: Slavic Expansion
description: Rapid expansion of Slavic-speaking peoples from their homeland in eastern Poland/western Ukraine across Central and Eastern Europe and the Balkans
consequences: Slavic languages becoming dominant across Eastern Europe; displacement of earlier populations; Christianization creating Catholic/Orthodox divide; development of Cyrillic and Latin-script Slavic traditions

name: German Eastward Settlement
description: Medieval German colonization and settlement eastward into Slavic and Baltic territories
consequences: Germanization of formerly Slavic areas; establishment of Hanseatic trade cities; Teutonic Order state in Prussia; lasting German-Slavic linguistic and cultural boundaries

name: Dutch Colonial Maritime Network
description: Dutch East India Company maritime empire connecting the Netherlands to southern Africa, South and Southeast Asia, and the East Indies
consequences: Development of Afrikaans; Indonesian Malay as trade language; Cape Colony settlement; spice monopoly; colonial legacy across Southeast Asia; creole languages in former Dutch territories

name: British Colonial Expansion in Africa
description: British colonial expansion across Africa from West Africa to East Africa and Southern Africa
consequences: Spread of English as official language; creation of colonial borders dividing ethnic groups; introduction of British legal and educational systems; independence movements; Commonwealth ties

name: French Colonial Expansion in Africa
description: French colonial expansion across North and West Africa, establishing French West Africa and French Equatorial Africa
consequences: Francophone Africa; French as official language across numerous nations; Negritude literary movement; decolonization struggles; Organisation internationale de la Francophonie

name: Austronesian Indian Ocean Crossing
description: Remarkable maritime migration of Austronesian peoples from Borneo across the Indian Ocean to settle Madagascar
consequences: Malagasy language closely related to Ma'anyan of Borneo despite 6000km separation; cultural blend of Southeast Asian and East African traditions; outrigger canoe technology

name: Thule Inuit Arctic Migration
description: Migration of Thule Inuit peoples from Alaska eastward across the Canadian Arctic to Greenland
consequences: Replacement of earlier Dorset culture; adaptation of whale-hunting technology; Inuit languages spread across Arctic; cultural continuity from Alaska to Greenland

name: Transatlantic European Migration
description: Mass European emigration to the Americas during the 19th and early 20th centuries
consequences: Transformation of American demographics; Ellis Island and immigration culture; ethnic neighborhoods in American cities; multicultural society formation; brain drain from Europe

name: Indian Indenture System Migration
description: Migration of Indian indentured laborers to British colonies after abolition of slavery, including Caribbean, Fiji, South Africa, and Mauritius
consequences: Indian diaspora communities worldwide; Hindu and Muslim communities in Caribbean and Pacific; Indo-Caribbean culture; Indian influence on cuisine, religion, and languages in host countries

name: Chinese Diaspora
description: Mass emigration of Chinese workers and merchants to Southeast Asia, the Americas, and worldwide
consequences: Chinatowns in major world cities; Chinese cultural influence in Southeast Asia; coolie trade; development of overseas Chinese business networks; Chinese diaspora maintaining cultural identity

name: Partition of India Migration
description: Mass population exchange between India and Pakistan at independence, with approximately 15 million displaced
consequences: Largest mass migration in human history; Hindu-Muslim demographic reshaping of South Asia; creation of distinct Hindi and Urdu literary traditions; trauma shaping India-Pakistan relations

name: European Scramble for Africa
description: Rapid European colonization of nearly all of Africa following the Berlin Conference of 1884-85
consequences: Arbitrary colonial borders dividing ethnic groups; imposition of European languages; destruction of indigenous political systems; resource extraction; lasting economic and political consequences for African nations

name: Tai Peoples Migration
description: Southward migration of Tai-speaking peoples from southern China into mainland Southeast Asia
consequences: Establishment of Thai and Lao kingdoms; displacement of Mon and Khmer populations; Theravada Buddhist culture; tonal language spread across mainland Southeast Asia

name: Melanesian Settlement
description: Ancient settlement of Melanesian islands by peoples from Southeast Asia, creating extraordinary linguistic diversity
consequences: Most linguistically diverse region on Earth with over 1000 languages; independent development of agriculture in New Guinea highlands; extreme linguistic fragmentation due to island geography

name: Moroccan Jewish Exodus
description: Mass emigration of Moroccan Jewish communities to Israel and France following Israeli independence and Arab-Israeli conflicts
consequences: End of centuries-old Jewish communities in Morocco; Mizrahi culture in Israel; preservation of Judeo-Arabic traditions; Moroccan Jewish diaspora in France and Canada

name: Alan Migration
description: Westward migration of the Iranian-speaking Alans, driven by the Huns, across Europe with the Vandals into Gaul and Iberia.
consequences: Alanic settlement in Iberia and Gaul; contribution to later Iberian populations

name: Amorite Migration
description: Movement of the Semitic-speaking Amorites from the Levant and Syria into Mesopotamia at the end of the third millennium BCE.
consequences: Amorite dynasties across Mesopotamia, including Old Babylon under Hammurabi

name: Anglo-Saxon Settlement of Britain
description: Migration and settlement of Angles, Saxons, and Jutes from the North Sea coast into lowland Britain after Roman withdrawal.
consequences: Emergence of the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms and the English language

name: Aramean Migration
description: Spread of the Semitic-speaking Arameans out of the Syrian steppe into the Levant and Mesopotamia.
consequences: Aramaic became the lingua franca of the Near East

name: Avar Migration
description: Migration of the Pannonian Avars from the Eurasian steppe into the Carpathian Basin, where they established the Avar Khaganate.
consequences: Reshaped Central European politics; pressure on Byzantium and the Franks

name: Bell Beaker Diffusion
description: Spread of the Bell Beaker cultural package across Western Europe, reaching Britain with substantial population replacement.
consequences: Near-complete genetic turnover in Britain; wide distribution of Beaker material culture

name: Bracero Program Migration
description: Managed labour migration of millions of Mexican farm workers (braceros) to the United States between 1942 and 1964.
consequences: Entrenched patterns of Mexican migration to US agriculture

name: Bulgar Migration
description: Dispersal of the Turkic Bulgars from Old Great Bulgaria on the Pontic steppe into the Balkans and the Volga region.
consequences: Foundation of the First Bulgarian Empire and Volga Bulgaria

name: Burgundian Migration
description: Migration of the Burgundians from the Baltic and Central Europe into the Rhône valley, founding the Kingdom of the Burgundians.
consequences: Burgundian settlement giving its name to the Burgundy region

name: California Gold Rush Migration
description: Mass migration of prospectors from across the world to the goldfields of northern California.
consequences: Explosive growth of San Francisco; California statehood; devastation of Native Californians

name: Cuman-Kipchak Migration
description: Migration of the Turkic Cuman-Kipchak confederation across the Eurasian steppe into the Pontic region and, after the Mongol conquest, into Hungary.
consequences: Dominance of the Cuman steppe (Desht-i Qipchaq); settlement in the Kingdom of Hungary

name: Dorian Invasion
description: Traditional account of the southward movement of Dorian Greeks into the Peloponnese after the Mycenaean collapse.
consequences: Redistribution of Greek dialects; Dorian settlement of Sparta and Crete

name: Dust Bowl Migration
description: Displacement of farming families from the drought-stricken southern Great Plains toward California during the 1930s.
consequences: Roughly 2.5 million left the Plains; reshaped Californian agriculture and politics

name: European Migrant Crisis
description: Surge of refugees and migrants, chiefly from Syria, crossing the Mediterranean and the Balkans into the European Union.
consequences: Political crisis over EU asylum policy; strain on the Schengen system

name: Fulani Expansion
description: Eastward pastoral expansion of the Fula (Fulani) people across the Sahel from Senegambia toward Lake Chad.
consequences: Spread of Islam and pastoralism; Fulani jihad states of the 18th–19th centuries

name: Great Trek
description: Eastward and northward migration of Dutch-descended Boer Voortrekkers from the British Cape Colony into the South African interior.
consequences: Foundation of the Boer republics; conflict with Zulu and Ndebele

name: Guanche Settlement of the Canary Islands
description: Settlement of the Canary Islands by Berber Guanche peoples from northwest Africa.
consequences: Isolated Neolithic-level society encountered by Europeans in the 14th–15th centuries

name: Huguenot Diaspora
description: Flight of French Calvinist Huguenots after the Revocation of the Edict of Nantes, into the Dutch Republic, England, Prussia, and the Cape.
consequences: Transfer of skills and capital out of France; Huguenot communities across Protestant Europe

name: Hunnic Migration
description: Westward movement of the nomadic Huns from the Central Asian steppe into the Pontic region and Pannonia, displacing Gothic and other Germanic peoples.
consequences: Triggered the Migration Period; pressured the Western Roman Empire

name: Hyksos Migration
description: Infiltration and settlement of West Semitic Hyksos peoples into the eastern Nile Delta, culminating in their rule as Egypt's Fifteenth Dynasty.
consequences: Introduced the composite bow and horse-drawn chariot to Egypt

name: Italian Diaspora
description: Large-scale emigration of Italians, especially to the Americas, from the late 19th to mid-20th centuries.
consequences: Major Italian communities in Argentina, Brazil, and the United States

name: Khazar Migration
description: Westward movement of the Turkic Khazars into the North Caucasus and lower Volga, where they built the Khazar Khaganate.
consequences: A powerful steppe state buffering Byzantium and the Caliphate; elite conversion to Judaism

name: Lombard Migration
description: Movement of the Lombards from Pannonia into the Italian peninsula, establishing the Lombard Kingdom in the Po Valley.
consequences: Fragmentation of Byzantine Italy; foundation of the Kingdom of the Lombards

name: Austronesian Settlement of Madagascar
description: Trans-Indian Ocean voyage of Austronesian seafarers from Borneo to Madagascar, the westernmost Austronesian settlement.
consequences: Austronesian language and crops (rice, banana) established off the African coast

name: Mariel Boatlift
description: Mass emigration of roughly 125,000 Cubans by boat from Mariel harbour to Florida in 1980.
consequences: Reshaped the Cuban-American community of South Florida

name: Mfecane
description: Period of widespread upheaval and forced migration among southern African peoples associated with the rise of the Zulu kingdom.
consequences: Depopulation and reorganisation of the interior; formation of new states (Sotho, Ndebele, Swazi)

name: Nabataean Migration
description: Movement of the nomadic Nabataean Arabs into the Transjordan and northern Arabia, settling around Petra.
consequences: Control of the incense trade; foundation of the Nabataean Kingdom

name: Nilotic Expansion
description: Southward migration of Nilotic pastoralist peoples from the southern Sudan into the East African Great Lakes region.
consequences: Spread of cattle pastoralism and Nilotic languages across East Africa

name: Oregon Trail Migration
description: Overland wagon migration of settlers from the Missouri River across the Great Plains and Rockies to the Oregon Country.
consequences: American settlement of the Pacific Northwest; displacement of Indigenous nations

name: Ostrogothic Migration
description: Movement of the Ostrogoths under Theodoric from Pannonia into Italy, where they overthrew Odoacer.
consequences: Foundation of the Ostrogothic Kingdom of Italy

name: 1948 Palestinian Exodus
description: Flight and expulsion of Palestinian Arabs during the 1948 Arab-Israeli War into neighbouring states and the West Bank and Gaza.
consequences: Creation of a long-term Palestinian refugee population; enduring regional conflict

name: Pecheneg Migration
description: Westward movement of the Turkic Pechenegs from Central Asia across the Pontic steppe to the frontiers of Kievan Rus and Byzantium.
consequences: Long conflict with Rus and Byzantium until defeat at Levounion

name: Phrygian Migration
description: Migration of the Phrygians from the southern Balkans across the straits into west-central Anatolia.
consequences: Foundation of the Kingdom of Phrygia centred on Gordion

name: Scythian Migration
description: Westward migration of the Iranian-speaking Scythians across the Eurasian steppe into the Pontic-Caspian region.
consequences: Formation of Scythian dominance over the Pontic steppe; contact with Greek colonies

name: Sea Peoples Migration
description: Movements of the seafaring Sea Peoples across the eastern Mediterranean, raiding Anatolia, the Levant, and Egypt at the close of the Bronze Age.
consequences: Contributed to the Late Bronze Age collapse; destruction of Hittite and Levantine cities

name: Sephardic Jewish Expulsion
description: Expulsion of Jews from Spain (1492) and Portugal (1497) and their dispersal across the Mediterranean and the Ottoman Empire.
consequences: Sephardic communities in the Ottoman lands, North Africa, and the Netherlands; spread of Ladino

name: Suebic Migration
description: Migration of the Suebi across the Rhine and through Gaul into northwestern Iberia, where they founded a kingdom in Galicia.
consequences: Kingdom of the Suebi (Gallaecia), among the first post-Roman Germanic states

name: Vandal Migration
description: Migration of the Vandals from Central Europe through Gaul and Iberia into Roman North Africa, where they founded a kingdom centred on Carthage.
consequences: Sack of Rome (455 CE); disruption of Roman grain supply

name: Vietnamese Boat People
description: Maritime flight of refugees from Vietnam after the fall of Saigon, across the South China Sea to Southeast Asian camps and resettlement abroad.
consequences: Large Vietnamese diaspora in the US, Australia, France, and Canada

name: Visigothic Migration
description: Migration of the Visigoths from the lower Danube through Italy and Gaul into Iberia, founding a kingdom centred on Toledo.
consequences: Sack of Rome (410 CE); the Visigothic Kingdom of Hispania

name: Volga German Migration
description: Migration of German colonists to the lower Volga region at the invitation of Catherine the Great.
consequences: Established the Volga German community, later deported under Stalin

name: Yamnaya Steppe Migration
description: Expansion of Yamnaya steppe herders from the Pontic-Caspian steppe into Central and Northern Europe, carrying steppe ancestry.
consequences: Major genetic turnover in Europe; associated with the spread of Indo-European languages
